item.title: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates
item.description: The pro-Israel lobbying group and influential political funder announced it would no longer endorse candidates or give directly to campaigns. AIPAC's affiliated super PAC, though, will continue.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The Justice Department begins notifying counties where it wants to monitor elections
item.description: The department has long deployed election monitors, but the Trump administration's unprecedented steps to try to wrestle control over elections have led to new concerns about DOJ monitoring this year.

item.title: Poll: Voters want Congress to be a check on Trump, trust Democrats more on issues
item.description: A new poll shows record support for Democratic congressional candidates ahead of the midterms, as voters feel the party is better attuned to handling their top issues.

item.title: Meet the people moving north to escape increasingly hot summers
item.description: As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?

item.description: The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

item.title: How Trump's attacks on voting system integrity might affect upcoming elections
item.description: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains Trump's interference in the midterms, including threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they strike alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.

item.title: Why local officials are feeling 'on edge' as election day approaches
item.description: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.

item.title: Supreme Court upholds pause on Trump's anti-trans prison policy
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration has to continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons as litigation on efforts to change the policy continues.

item.title: New human data hints at psychedelics' potential to combat inflammation
item.description: Lab studies have shown that psychedelics like psilocybin can lower inflammation and may be protective for a range of illnesses. Now, researchers are publishing some of the first data in humans that signals this holds potential for patients with neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease.
